title: selectedDate never advances at local midnight while the Fuel tab stays open
steps: Fake the clock to 2026-09-30 23:55 local, load /fuel, then advance the clock (no reload/navigation) to 2026-10-01 00:10. Open Add Food and log a manual entry.
expected: Once local time crosses midnight, the page either re-derives selectedDate to the new day or clearly shows the entry is being logged to the prior day before saving.
actual: The Add Food dialog still read "Logging to ... Sep 30" after the clock crossed into Oct 1, and the saved row's date column was 2026-09-30 (stale) while eaten_at correctly captured the real 2026-10-01T06:10:00Z instant. The entry is silently misattributed to the wrong day in daily/weekly totals with zero on-screen indication.
evidence: areas/fuel/scripts/r1-01.mjs console output (date=2026-09-30, eaten_at=2026-10-01T06:10:00+00:00, dialogHeader="Logging to Wed, Sep 30")
suspectFile: src/pages/FoodTracker.jsx:202 (selectedDate = useState(...) never re-derives from a live clock)
why: Re-ran r1-01: after crossing 23:55->00:10 with no reload the dialog still says 'Logging to Wed, Sep 30' and the row saved date=2026-09-30 while eaten_at=2026-10-01T06:10Z (00:10 MDT), so the row contradicts itself. selectedDate is only set once by useState(format(new Date())) at FoodTracker.jsx:203. The realistic trigger is the home-screen app resumed the next morning without a reload (iOS keeps a backgrounded PWA alive for hours), then breakfast logged to yesterday. Severity is really misattribution, not loss: the entry still exists on the prior day. The 'Logging to' header is a small cue but easy to miss. A code-only fix is small and needs no design call: only roll forward when the user was on today, and leave a deliberately chosen past day alone.
fixHint: src/pages/FoodTracker.jsx:203 - keep a ref of the 'today' string; on visibilitychange/focus (plus a 60s interval) recompute it, and if it changed and selectedDate === the old today, setSelectedDate(newToday).

title: Reloading /fuel mid-navigation surfaces an uncaught pageerror from an unrelated program_workouts fetch
steps: Same setup as fuel-r1-08 (edit an entry, click Save, then page.reload() ~150ms later). Captured via drive.mjs's pageerror listener.
expected: Navigating away mid-fetch should not surface an uncaught JS error to the console; in-flight requests being aborted by navigation is a normal browser event and should be handled/swallowed (e.g. by react-query's abort handling), not thrown.
actual: report() captured a pageerror: ".../rest/v1/program_workouts?select=*&program_id=in.(...) due to access control checks." This fired once during the reload in the r1-08 run. It is not about food_entries and may be a global app-shell query (training program prefetch) rather than anything Fuel-specific; flagging since it's an uncaught error a real user could also hit by reloading/navigating away from /fuel while that background fetch is in flight. Caveat: only observed once, under an artificially delayed-network test harness — worth a verify pass to confirm it reproduces under normal (undelayed) network conditions too.
evidence: areas/fuel/scripts/r1-08.mjs report() output: problems=[{"type":"pageerror","msg":".../program_workouts?select=*&program_id=in.(...) due to access control checks."}]
suspectFile: unknown — likely a global training-plan query hook active on the app shell, not src/pages/FoodTracker.jsx itself
why: Harness artifact. My r1-08 re-run showed no such error. The same pageerror did appear in my r1-04 re-run with no reload at all, so its source is drive.mjs start(), which does a full page.goto('/today') and then page.goto('/fuel') 2.5s later. That aborts /today's in-flight useEnrollments query (src/hooks/useProgramQueries.js:65-68, select * on program_workouts). WebKit reports an aborted fetch as 'due to access control checks'. On the phone the app opens on one route and moves between screens by SPA navigation, which never aborts that fetch. Nothing reaches the user, and it is not Fuel code.

title: Add Food dialog fields get hidden behind the on-screen keyboard (iOS-layer warning)
steps: Open Add Food / Manual entry and focus #food_name or #calories on the simulated iPhone viewport.
expected: Per judge rule, iPhone-layer warnings (field hidden by keyboard) count as ios bugs and should be fixed (e.g. scroll-into-view / dialog resize on keyboard open).
actual: drive.mjs's report() recorded a recurring field-hidden-by-keyboard warning across multiple cases (seen on #calories in r1-02's run and #food_name in r1-06's run): "Focused field is covered by the keyboard or pushed under the status bar." This also caused real test-flow friction: taps on controls below an autofocused field are silently swallowed unless the keyboard is dismissed first (worked around in every script via dismissKeyboard()), which is exactly the kind of confusion a real user would hit too.
repro: ui-audit/overnight/areas/fuel/scripts/r1-02.mjs, r1-06.mjs (see report() output in each run)
suspectFile: src/pages/FoodTracker.jsx (Add Food dialog layout/scroll handling around the search/manual-entry fields)
why: Rejected: the warning comes from the simulator, not the app. The app never scrolls on focus itself: FoodTracker.jsx and the ui Input have no scrollIntoView or onFocus scroll handler. The only movement comes from the browser and the iphone-sim layer. What I ran against the current layer: (1) scripts/v1-ios.mjs taps #food_name, #calories and #protein one at a time with the keyboard dismissed in between. Every field lands at y=251, above the keyboard top of 513, with 0 warnings. (2) scripts/v1-ios4.mjs leaves the keyboard up. #food_name lands at 251 and #protein at 250, both clean. #calories sits at y=634 before the move, under the keyboard, because it is the field right below the one being typed in. A thumb can't tap it there. Tapping at 634 hits the keyboard picture, and the real way there is the accessory 'next' button. Moving focus that way, which is what the layer's moveFocus -> el.focus() does, leaves #calories at y=544, still covered, and raises the warning. That is the layer's model breaking down. In showKeyboard (iphone-sim/layer.js:219-233) it reveals a field only by window.scrollBy plus a visual-viewport pan capped at baseH - vvHeight (413px). It never scrolls the fixed sheet's own overflow container. Here the dialog is a position:fixed sheet with an inner scroller, so window scroll does nothing and the pan hits its cap. Real iOS 26 WebKit reveals a focused input through the enclosing overflow scroll areas (scrollRectToVisible) before panning, so the sheet would scroll calories above the keyboard. The warnings in r1-02, r1-06 and r1-09 come from the same path: Playwright fill() on a field below the keyboard, which gives different results for the same steps (field at y=168 with no warning in v1-ios2.mjs, y=-245 with a warning in v1-ios3.mjs). The 'taps swallowed under the autofocused search keyboard' friction isn't an app bug either. Radix focuses the search field from an effect, outside the tap's synchronous handler, so standalone iOS usually won't raise the keyboard there. When it does, covering controls below it is normal iOS. Worth one on-device check: accessory-next from Food Name to Calories in Add Food. If Calories stays covered on the real phone, the fix is a cheap onFocus scrollIntoView({block:'center'}) on the dialog's inputs.

title: Offline manual add — form state preserved for retry, no false success
steps: Open Add Food, fill a manual entry, go offline (context.setOffline(true)), tap Add Food, wait, then go back online.
expected: No false success while offline; form values preserved; clear error feedback telling the athlete what happened and what to do; exactly one row exists once back online (no drop, no duplicate).
actual: Data integrity was fine: no false success while offline, the dialog and its form values (name, calories) stayed intact, and exactly one row existed once reconnected with no retap needed. But there was NO error feedback at all while offline — the Add Food button gets stuck reading "Adding..." indefinitely with no "Failed to log food" toast, because Chromium/Playwright offline emulation (and likely real airplane-mode/no-signal conditions) leaves the underlying fetch pending rather than rejecting it, so the mutation's onError never fires and there is no timeout to catch it. An athlete at the gym with no signal has no way to know whether to wait, retry, or that anything is wrong.
evidence: areas/fuel/scripts/r1-09.mjs console output: sawFalseSuccess=false stuckAdding=true sawFailureToast=false rowsWhileOffline=0 rowsAfterReconnect=1
suspectFile: src/pages/FoodTracker.jsx:1115-1117 (addFoodMutation onError only fires on an actual rejected request; no client-side timeout for a stalled fetch)
why: Re-ran r1-09: offline, the button stays on 'Adding...' indefinitely with no message; on reconnect exactly 1 row is saved. The attacker blamed a fetch that never rejects. The actual cause is React Query v5's default networkMode 'online' (App.jsx:58 new QueryClient() with defaults): while navigator.onLine is false the mutation is paused, not failed, and it resumes on reconnect. Real iOS airplane mode or no signal flips navigator.onLine the same way, so the stuck state is real at the gym. Data is safe only while the app stays open. The fix is just an honest label.
fixHint: src/pages/FoodTracker.jsx:3154 - when addFoodMutation.isPaused (or updateFoodMutation.isPaused), show 'Offline - saves when you're back online' instead of 'Adding...' (optionally let the dialog close, since the paused mutation resumes on its own).

title: Re-approve the week plan after manually editing one planned item's amount
steps: Edit a planned item's (Eggs) amount via the entry editor, save, then tap 'Approve & load the week' again on the same week.
expected: Either the manual edit survives the re-approve, or the athlete is warned before it would be discarded.
actual: The manual edit was silently discarded with no warning: the row was recreated with the algorithm's originally-computed serving_size, losing the athlete's hand correction entirely. No confirm/warning dialog appeared before the discard.
suspectFile: src/components/nutrition/WeeklyPlanCard.jsx approve mutation — unconditional delete().eq("planned", true).in("date", dates) before recreating from resolveDayPlan(), with no diff/check against hand-edited rows
why: Re-ran r1-11. The script's UI edit came back as 425 instead of the 516 typed. I isolated that in scripts/v1-edit.mjs, and it is not locator flakiness. The right Amount field showed 516 at blur and at the Save click, and no input events fired. Yet a planned row saved serving_size 438 (runs gave 412, 436 and 438) while serving_grams was 516. A non-planned row given the identical edit saves exactly 516. The cause is src/hooks/usePlannedDayRebalance.js:80-95, which by design rescales every remaining planned row so eaten + planned lands on the day's calorie target, and it immediately overwrites a hand-edited planned amount. Re-approve (WeeklyPlanCard.jsx:214-226: delete all planned rows for the week, then re-insert) then discards whatever is left: the re-run turned the 516 g Eggs row into a new id at 145 g, with no warning. Both behaviors are intentional (the code comments say so), but together they mean the athlete cannot pin a planned portion; typed amounts silently change. Which behavior is right is Nolan's call: (a) warn/confirm on re-approve, plus a note in the edit dialog for planned items ('planned amounts auto-fit your daily target'), which is code-only; (b) pin hand-edited planned rows, which needs an 'edited'/'pinned' column, so a hosted migration and a proposal; (c) keep as is.
fixHint: src/components/nutrition/WeeklyPlanCard.jsx:557: before approve.mutate(), if planned rows already exist for `dates`, confirm('Replace this week's N planned items? Hand edits will be reset.'). For edit-stickiness, src/hooks/usePlannedDayRebalance.js:80 would need to skip pinned rows, which needs a new column (migration, proposal).

title: Carb-cycled targets and shopping list across a week-boundary approve (Sunday into next week)
steps: Fake the clock to a future Sunday, approve the week plan, advance the clock into Monday via SPA navigation (no reload), and check planned rows/UI state.
expected: The full week's planned rows commit atomically (or the failure/success reporting accurately reflects what did and didn't commit); the carb-cycled figures and grocery list stay correct.
actual: Reproduced on three separate runs: the approve mutation's Promise.all over ~40+ parallel food_entries .create() calls (one per planned row across the week) hit a 429 on auth/v1/token?grant_type=refresh_token partway through. Every .create() still in flight after that failed with 401 -> RLS policy violation, while creates that had already completed stayed committed. Result: Sunday and Monday (the first two days processed) each got their full 6 rows, but 2026-11-03..2026-11-07 got zero — the week was left silently, partially populated — while the mutation as a whole reports failure to the user (onError / a failure toast) with no indication of which days did or didn't load. This is a genuine non-atomic-bulk-write architecture risk independent of the specific 429 trigger (plausibly this test harness's own heavy repeated-login pattern rather than a realistic single-user scenario) — any transient per-row failure would produce the same silent partial commit. The originally-suspected carb-cycle-text/grocery-list staleness question did not reproduce as a bug: WeeklyPlanCard recomputes today/dates live from the clock every render, so text changing across the Sun->Monday crossing is expected, correct behavior.
evidence: areas/fuel/scripts/r1-12.mjs console output: sunRows=6 monRows=6 sawPartialCommitCascade=true, plus captured 429/401 HTTP problems and 'new row violates row-level security policy for table "food_entries"' console errors for dates 2026-11-03..2026-11-07
suspectFile: src/components/nutrition/WeeklyPlanCard.jsx approve mutation — await Promise.all(rows.map((r) => db.entities.FoodEntry.create(r))) has no per-row error isolation, no rollback of rows that DID succeed when a sibling create fails, and no partial-success reporting
why: Re-ran r1-12: reproduced a partial week (Sun 7 rows, Mon 7, the rest missing) behind a 'Couldn't load the plan' toast. The trigger here is a harness artifact. startWithClock fakes Date to 2026-11-01, five weeks ahead, so every real access token looks expired. The ~40 parallel creates at WeeklyPlanCard.jsx:226 each attempt a refresh, and the flood of refreshes returns 429, then 401s and RLS errors. On a phone with a real clock supabase-js shares one refresh, so this 429 cascade won't happen. The underlying shape is still real: 40 separate inserts after an unchecked delete, so a flaky gym network dropping some requests leaves a partly loaded week. It isn't data loss: planned rows are regenerated, eaten rows are untouched, the error toast shows, and tapping Approve again (delete + recreate) heals it. Downgraded to minor. The fix is cheap: one request, and a single PostgREST insert is atomic.
fixHint: src/components/nutrition/WeeklyPlanCard.jsx:214-226 - check the delete's { error } and replace the Promise.all of creates with one `const { error } = await supabase.from('food_entries').insert(rows); if (error) throw error;` (atomic, 1 request instead of ~40).

title: Log a recipe at 9999 servings — no upper bound on LogRecipeDialog
steps: Seed a recipe directly in the DB using the recipes table's real column names (calories/protein_grams/carbs_grams/fats_grams), log it via the UI's LogRecipeDialog at servingCount=9999.
expected: An implausible serving count is blocked or requires confirmation; at minimum, macros scale correctly and are never corrupted.
actual: Worse than the servings-upper-bound question: scaleRecipeToServings() (src/utils/nutritionUtils.js) reads recipe.total_calories/total_protein/total_carbs/total_fats, but the recipes table's actual columns (confirmed against the migration schema and live insert probing) are calories/protein_grams/carbs_grams/fats_grams. Any real recipe row therefore scales to NaN, logged as a food_entries row with calories=null (a React console NaN warning fires) — at ANY serving count, not just 9999. Separately, and consistent with the same naming bug, RecipeBuilder.jsx's RecipeFormDialog.handleSave() INSERTs total_calories/total_protein/total_carbs/total_fats into recipes, which has no such columns — confirmed live via a direct probe returning PGRST204 "Could not find the 'total_calories' column of 'recipes' in the schema cache" on every attempted recipe creation. Net effect: recipe creation via the UI wizard fails every time, and even a recipe present in the table (e.g. seeded directly) logs with corrupted null/NaN macros when used. The servings field itself has no max (min="0.5" step="0.5") but that is secondary to the schema mismatch.
evidence: areas/fuel/scripts/r1-13.mjs console output: disabledAt9999=false rowsCreated=1 corruptedRow=true calories=null reactNanWarning=true; plus a live PGRST204 probe on RecipeFormDialog.handleSave's field names
suspectFile: src/utils/nutritionUtils.js:79-98 (calculateRecipeTotals / scaleRecipeToServings) and src/components/nutrition/RecipeBuilder.jsx:993-1017 (handleSave) — both use total_calories/total_protein/total_carbs/total_fats naming that does not match the recipes table's real columns
why: Confirmed against the real schema and live. supabase/migrations/00000000000000_remote_schema.sql:720-732 defines recipes with calories/protein_grams/carbs_grams/fats_grams, and no later migration touches recipes. My live probe inserting total_calories returned PGRST204 'Could not find the total_calories column of recipes'. Re-running r1-13, a correctly shaped recipe logged at 9999 servings wrote calories=null, with a React NaN warning. So creating a recipe in the UI always fails, and logging any existing recipe corrupts its macros at any serving count. No migration is needed: the table already has the right columns, and the fix is renaming on the client. calculateRecipeTotals also feeds the builder's on-screen totals (RecipeBuilder.jsx:389-441), so keep its return shape and map only at the DB boundary. The 9999 upper bound is secondary; the r1-05 plausibility confirm covers it.
fixHint: src/components/nutrition/RecipeBuilder.jsx:1009 - replace ...calculateRecipeTotals(...) with const t = calculateRecipeTotals(...); calories: t.total_calories, protein_grams: t.total_protein, carbs_grams: t.total_carbs, fats_grams: t.total_fats; and src/utils/nutritionUtils.js:94-97 - read recipe.calories ?? recipe.total_calories (same for protein_grams/carbs_grams/fats_grams).

title: Barcode scan: product not found, then label-photo fallback — form isn't silently pre-filled with stale scan data
steps: Open Add Food, tap Scan barcode (no real camera hardware in this environment, so getUserMedia fails and BarcodeScanner.jsx lands on scanState="error" rather than "not_found" — both share the identical onNotFound(foundBarcode) wiring), tap Enter manually, then reopen the scanner a second time and repeat.
expected: The search field never accumulates/leaks stale text across attempts, the scanner starts fresh each reopen, and any error message accurately reflects what happened.
actual: The state-reset and search-field-cleanliness concerns did NOT reproduce as bugs: the scanner starts a genuinely fresh attempt on each reopen and the search field never accumulates stale text. But a real, confirmed bug was found: "Enter manually" from the camera-unavailable error state fires the exact same toast as the not_found path — "Product not found. Try searching manually." — even though no scan or lookup ever happened (the camera never started). FoodTracker.jsx's onNotFound handler is shared, unconditional, single-message code for both states. This tells the athlete their product wasn't found when in fact nothing was ever looked up. NOTE (scope caveat): with no real camera in this environment, the not_found state itself and the 'Photograph the label' -> onScanLabel fallback (not_found-only) were not directly exercised; source-level cross-check of onNotFound's overwrite-not-append semantics found no separate accumulation bug on that untested path either.
evidence: areas/fuel/scripts/r1-15.mjs console output: sawErrorState1=true sawMisleadingNotFoundToast=true cleanReset=true searchFieldClean=true noPageErrors=true
